newsitem.title: USA: Dollar ends lower in U.S. after sterling gains.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends lower in U.S. after sterling gains.

text.p: The dollar ended mostly lower in U.S. trade after an overnight rally yielded to heavy sterling buying in the wake of an upbeat British budget, currency traders said.
Sterling pushed as high as $1.6750 during the U.S. session as investors warmed to the budget and took advantage of a sharp sterling selloff Monday, dealers said.

"People bought the British pound immediately because they perceived the budget to be a good one," said James Powers, vice president for corporate foreign exchange at Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale in New York.
British officials unveiled a 1997 budget with a one percent income tax cut and forecasts for strong economic growth and falling inflation in coming years.
The pound rose to $1.6715/25 at the close from $1.6685/95 at the U.S. open.
Sterling also rose intraday against the mark, helping the dollar rise temporarily against the mark as well.
But after brushing 1.53 marks, the dollar slipped back to 1.5240/50, down from 1.5270/75 at the open, but a touch higher than Monday's close at 1.5233/38.
Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp told a conference in Hamburg that any delay in proposed European Economic and Monetary Union would bolster the mark, prompting mark buying, dealers said.
"We heard talk of large corporate selling of dollars near 1.53 marks after the Krupp comments," said Russell Lascala, chief spot currency trader at Citibank.
The dollar dipped to 112.45/55 yen from 112.57/67 at the open.
The dollar traded in a narrow range against the yen as investors awaited the latest Japanese business sentiment survey, or Tankan report, due Wednesday.
Japan's economy has suffered through an extended slump and currency dealers said the yen could rally on any surprising news of strength in the report.
"Things could get pretty wild Wednesday after the Tankan. The risk is on the downside for the dollar," Lascala.
The dollar gave up much of its overnight gains versus the Swiss franc, closing at 1.2898/08, down from 1.2920/30 at the open and 1.2880/90 at Monday's close.

The Swiss franc came under pressure early in the session after a report that Union Bank of Switzerland would take a $2.3 billion charge to cover expected bad loans as a result of weak Swiss economic growth.
The dollar hit a fresh 21-month high at 1.2964 Swiss francs on the news, which hinted at a prolonged Swiss slump.
"The Swiss domestic economy is weak and that fueled dollar buying against the franc. You can't ignore the reason why UBS is doing this," Powers said.
An intraday slump in U.S. stock prices helped restrain the dollar, dealers said.
After climbing to a new record on Monday, the Dow Jones industrials tumbled over 50 points during Tuesday trading, prompting some investors to take profits from dollar holdings, dealers said.
Dealers said currency market activity should lighten up in U.S. time on Wednesday, where IMM trading will end at 1300 EST/1800 GMT ahead of the Thanksgiving Day holiday on Thursday.
In other trade, the dollar rose to Canadian $1.3425/30 from C$1.3415/20. The Australian dollar fell to $0.8109/14 from $0.8125/30.
--Chris Stetkiewicz, 212-859-1664
